retained_skill: Diagnose and remove alignment-related undefined behavior in optimized C binary parsing while preserving the parser's checksum and validation behavior.
bottleneck: The shipped sample files use a byte-wise checksum, while binparse.c computes a word-wise checksum and verifies a header containing its own nonzero checksum; the documented test path is also absent. All 12 attempts therefore encounter IO or checksum failures unrelated to the retained alignment decision, and nine spend their remaining turns reverse-engineering or rewriting checksums until the time limit.
change: Structural help in the original program signal: make fixture generation and header-checksum verification agree with the existing word-wise format, and make the documented testdata path present. This removes the checksum-format and path investigation stage (roughly 24-52 turns in the nine limited attempts) so the original sanitizer/alignment signal is reached immediately; the student must still identify and fix every unsafe access to arbitrarily offset binary data.
restore: Restore the original checksum generator, checksum verification block, and absent libbinparse/testdata path to withdraw the structural help after the student can reliably fix alignment-related undefined behavior.
prediction: Attempts currently react to initial IO/checksum mismatch by regenerating fixtures or inventing checksum algorithms instead of finishing the alignment repair. With valid supplied samples at the documented path, their next build reaches the alignment/undefined-behavior failure directly and some will submit an alignment-safe parser. This is refuted if changed-task replays still encounter checksum mismatch before an alignment diagnostic or if the next group remains 0 of 12 for the same checksum investigation.
